items.title: Origami
items.short: Traditional Japanese paper folding in which a simple sheet becomes animals, flowers and other decorative forms.
items.description:
Origami is the traditional Japanese art of paper folding. A single sheet of paper can be transformed without cutting into many shapes, from simple animals and flowers to more complex decorative objects.

Participants will learn the basic principles of origami and, with guidance from the instructors, create several paper models step by step.

The workshop is suitable for complete beginners and children. No previous experience is required.

items.title: Shodō – Japanese calligraphy
items.short: A practical workshop in traditional Japanese calligraphy introducing brush, ink and the basic principles of writing Japanese characters.
items.description:
Shodō (書道), literally “the way of writing”, is the traditional Japanese art of calligraphy. It combines precise movement and the use of brush, ink and paper with concentration and the aesthetics of each stroke.

Participants will learn about the basic tools used in Japanese calligraphy, correct brush handling and the fundamentals of individual strokes.

With guidance from the instructors, they will then try writing simple Japanese characters and create their own piece of calligraphy.

The workshop is suitable for complete beginners. No knowledge of Japanese or calligraphy is required.

items.title: Japanese fabric button making
items.short: A workshop making original decorative buttons from Japanese fabrics.
items.description:
Participants will make their own decorative button from fabrics with Japanese patterns under the guidance of Aiko Bosák.

Aiko Bosák will also have kimono available for sale at the event.

items.title: Tsumami zaiku つまみ細工
items.short: A creative tsumami zaiku workshop using craft plates.
items.description: Hisayo Yasuda will introduce tsumami zaiku using special tsumami zaiku craft plates. Participants can try folding fabric into small decorative motifs.

items.title: Ayatori あやとり
items.short: A traditional Japanese string-loop game in which the fingers create different patterns and figures.
items.description:
Ayatori is a traditional Japanese game played with a loop of string or cord. Using the fingers, players create different patterns and figures that can gradually transform from one shape into another.

The game is especially familiar to children in Japan, but its many techniques and difficulty levels also make it enjoyable for adults. It develops fine motor skills, concentration, memory and hand coordination.

Participants will learn the basic techniques and try creating several traditional ayatori patterns.

The workshop is free.

Maximum capacity is 10 participants.
